newsitem.title: USA: Security-Connecticut Q4 life sales down.
newsitem.headline: Security-Connecticut Q4 life sales down.

text.p: Security-Connecticut Corp said fourth quarter life insurance sales fell 25 percent compared with a strong year ago quarter and rose 5.6 percent in 1996 compared with a year ago.

"The major term life insurance players slashed their prices to gain market share, and new universal life policies were introduced into an already- overserved estate-planning market," Security-Connecticut chief executive Ronald Jarvis said.
"We have been repositioning our products, and we think life sales will improve markedly later this year."
Security-Connecticut said annuity sales in 1996 were down 46 percent compared to the previous year.

"In an environment characterized by low interest rates and a relatively flat yield curve, fixed-annuity sales were down substantially industry-wide and were displaced by an increase in variable annuity sales," Jarvis said.
"In this environment, we held to the disciplined strategy of maintaining our margins rather than sacrificing profitability to increase sales," he said.
Security-Connecticut said it is planning to introduce new products in 1997.
Next month, the company is scheduled to launch an equity-indexed annuity portfolio and, later in the year, an equity-indexed universal life portfolio, the company said.
The company earlier reported fourth quarter operating earnings of $0.89 a share compared with $0.19 a share a year ago. That was in line with analysts' First Call estimate.
For the full year, operating income was $3.55 a share compared with $2.34 a year ago.

Fourth quarter and full year results benefited from lower life claims and a decrease to the guaranty fund assessment liability. That was partially offset by higher litigation and deferred acquisition costs.
